## Findings

**Store scope:** Harbor Outfitters has 4 stores. S1 (Harbor), S2 (Midtown), and S3 (Eastgate) all opened 2025-01-01. S4 (Northside) opened 2025-07-01 and has no sales before that date, so it wasn't open during the year-earlier window at all. Per the "open in both periods" rule, only S1, S2, S3 are included; S4 is excluded.

**Basis:** gross sales (qty × unit price) from `sales_n`, attributed to `rang_up_at` (the store that rang up the sale), summed over each twelve-week window.

### Accounting weeks (Sunday–Saturday)
- Current: Sun 2026-04-05 through Sat 2026-06-27 → **$81,625.85** (633 lines)
- Year earlier: Sun 2025-04-06 through Sat 2025-06-28 → **$101,597.06** (801 lines)
- Change: **-19.66%**

### Operations weeks (Saturday–Friday)
- Current: Sat 2026-04-04 through Fri 2026-06-26 → **$81,043.97** (633 lines)
- Year earlier: Sat 2025-04-05 through Fri 2025-06-27 → **$101,272.82** (797 lines)
- Change: **-19.97%**

Note on windowing: "twelve full weeks ending Saturday 27 June 2026" lines up naturally as an accounting week (which ends on Saturday). Because operations weeks run Saturday-to-Friday, the last full operations week before Sat 27 Jun actually ends Fri 26 Jun 2026, so that convention's window is shifted one day earlier at both ends; each period is still 84 days, and the year-ago window is the same convention 52 weeks (364 days) prior, which preserves the day-of-week alignment.

Both conventions agree closely (about a 20% decline), so the answer is not sensitive to which week convention is used.

ANSWER: No, we are not growing: gross sales at stores open in both periods (S1, S2, S3) fell about 20% year over year for the twelve full weeks ending 27 June 2026, whether measured on accounting weeks (Sun-Sat, -19.66%) or operations weeks (Sat-Fri, -19.97%).
